seo.title: Google Business Profile Photos: Sizes and Tips
seo.meta_description: Google Business Profile photos and videos for Anaheim and Orange County businesses: sizes, formats, logo, cover photo, review status and what to shoot.

h1: Google Business Profile Photos and Videos: Sizes, Rules and What to Upload
answer: Google Business Profile photos help customers recognize and choose your business. Google accepts JPG or PNG files between 10 KB and 5 MB, recommends 720 by 720 pixels, and wants photos that are in focus, well lit and not heavily filtered. Videos can run up to 30 seconds. Anaheim and Orange County businesses should add a logo, cover photo, exterior, interior, team and work photos, all real.
key_takeaways: Use JPG or PNG, 10 KB to 5 MB.
New uploads can take 24 to 48 hours to appear.

sections.heading: Why photos matter
sections.body_html: Google's help page says photos and videos help complete your Business Profile and make it more attractive to customers, and that an exterior photo helps customers recognize your business when they visit. For a restaurant in Anaheim's Resort District or a contractor in Irvine, real photos are often what tips a searcher from comparing to calling.

sections.heading: Verify first
sections.body_html: Google notes that your photos and videos show up on Google only after you verify your Business Profile. If uploads appear stuck, check your verification status before anything else.

sections.heading: Photo specifications
sections.body_html: Google lists these standards: JPG or PNG format; between 10 KB and 5 MB; a recommended resolution of 720 pixels tall and 720 pixels wide; a minimum of 250 by 250 pixels. Photos should be in focus and well lit, with no significant alterations or excessive filters. In Google's words, the image should represent reality.

sections.heading: Video specifications
sections.body_html: Videos can be up to 30 seconds long and up to 75 MB, at a resolution of 720p or higher. Short clips of your space, your team at work or a finished project work well.

sections.heading: Logo and cover photo
sections.body_html: A logo helps customers recognize your business, and Google highlights it for businesses that have basic information such as a phone number and hours. A cover photo sits at the top of the profile, though Google notes that setting one does not guarantee it will show as the first image.

sections.heading: What to photograph
sections.body_html:
• The exterior from the street, so people recognize you on arrival.
  • The interior or workspace.
  • Your team, with permission.
  • Products, menu items or finished jobs.
  • Vehicles and equipment for service-area businesses.
  • Parking and entrances if they are hard to find.

Update photos regularly; newest media appears first on your profile.

sections.heading: How to upload
sections.body_html: On a computer, search for your business name and city in Google Search or Maps, then select Photos and Add photos. You can upload several at once. Businesses with 10 or more locations can bulk upload photos through a spreadsheet.

sections.heading: Upload status
sections.body_html: Google reviews each upload. Pending means it is still processing or your profile is not verified; Not approved means it was flagged for breaking policies; Live means customers can see it. Google says it can take 24 to 48 hours for photos and videos to show.

sections.heading: Customer photos
sections.body_html: Customers can add photos too. You cannot control all of them, but you can request removal of customer photos that break Google's policies. The best answer to poor customer photos is a steady flow of good ones of your own.

sections.heading: Photos, your website and AI
sections.body_html: Use the same real photos on your website with descriptive file names and alt text. Consistent, real imagery across your profile and site helps people trust what they see, and gives AI assistants and Google's systems more context about your business.

sections.heading: Photo checklist
sections.body_html:
• Profile verified.
  • Logo uploaded.
  • Cover photo chosen.
  • Exterior photo from the street.
  • Interior or workspace photos.
  • Team photos with permission.
  • Photos of products, dishes or finished jobs.
  • JPG or PNG, 10 KB to 5 MB, around 720 by 720 pixels.
  • No heavy filters or misleading edits.
  • A short video of 30 seconds or less.

sections.heading: A simple monthly photo routine
sections.body_html: Set a recurring reminder to add a handful of new photos each month. Take them on a phone in good daylight: the storefront as customers approach it, the space on a typical day, the team at work and a few recent products or projects. Check each image is sharp and honest before uploading. Over a year, a routine like this builds a large, current gallery that reflects how the business really looks, which helps people arriving from Google Maps recognize you and reduces surprises when they visit.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a nail salon near the Anaheim Packing District. Its profile starts with only a logo. The owner adds an exterior shot showing the entrance and nearby parking, interior photos of the stations, photos of finished nail designs taken under natural light and a 20-second video walking through the salon. A month later, new photos of seasonal designs are added. Customers searching on Maps now see what the salon looks like and the style of work it does before they book.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: It helps to see where this sits in the bigger picture. Google ranks local results mainly on relevance, distance and popularity, and AI assistants lean on the same public information: your Business Profile, your website, other listings and what customers write. For a business in Anaheim or anywhere in Orange County, the most reliable plan is simple and repeated: keep every listing accurate, explain each service clearly on its own page, show real proof of your work and reply to customers. Small improvements here compound, and they are far harder for competitors to copy than an ad budget.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Upload a logo and cover photo.
  2. Take exterior and interior photos in daylight.
  3. Add photos of recent work or products.
  4. Record one 30-second video.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: You do not need an agency for every step here; Google documents most of it clearly. Consider outside help when the work is urgent and unfamiliar, when you manage several locations, or when the same issue returns after you fix it. Ask any provider to show you the specific guideline or documentation behind each recommendation, to keep you as the owner of your accounts and to report results in calls, bookings and leads rather than vanity numbers. That is how Chimera works with Orange County businesses from our base in Anaheim.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Verify, then upload real, well-lit JPG or PNG photos around 720 pixels square, plus short videos, and keep adding new ones. Chimera, based in Anaheim, builds photo plans into Orange County profile work.

faqs.q: What size should Google Business Profile photos be?
faqs.a: Google recommends 720 by 720 pixels, with a minimum of 250 by 250, as JPG or PNG between 10 KB and 5 MB.
They show only after verification, and new uploads can take 24 to 48 hours.

faqs.q: Can I add videos to my profile?
faqs.a: Yes, up to 30 seconds and 75 MB at 720p or higher.

faqs.q: Can I use edited or filtered photos?
faqs.a: Google asks for photos without significant alterations or excessive filters.

faqs.q: Will my cover photo always show first?
faqs.a: Not necessarily; Google says it is not guaranteed.
You can request removal of customer photos that break Google's policies.
